data.standardized_narrative: Syndicate 1910's opening gross claims reserves were GBP 322.1m at 1 January 2018. Analysis of the gross claims development triangle indicates a small net strengthening on prior years of approximately GBP 1.9m (c.0.6% of opening reserves), with adverse movement concentrated in the 2015-2016 underwriting years partially offset by releases in older years. The report also notes an overall (deterioration)/improvement figure of GBP 11.6m (ambiguous/net) and highlights significant reinsurance activity (including reinsurance-to-close and sizable reinsurance acceptances) which materially affects reported recoverables and can distort direct reserve comparisons.
raw_causal_phrases: In 2018, there has been an overall (deterioration)/improvement of GBP 11.6m (2017: GBP 38.5m).
Reinsurance acceptances includes the reinsurance to close premium of GBP 38.6m received from the 2015 year of account of Syndicate 1910.
The principal assumption underlying the liability estimates is that the future claims development will follow a similar pattern to past claims development experience.

data.data_quality_notes: Prior-year development figure reported here (GBP 1.9m) is calculated from the gross claims development triangle (page 31) by comparing current estimates to the previous diagonal and excluding the two most recent underwriting years (2017-2018). The report also contains an ambiguous narrative statement of an "overall (deterioration)/improvement of GBP 11.6m" which appears to be a net (likely after reinsurance) measure and conflicts with the triangle-derived gross movement; that sentence has been captured verbatim under exact_reserve_text. Reinsurance-to-close and large reinsurance acceptances are present in the year and materially affect reinsurers' share and inter-year comparisons; this can distort simple year-on-year outstanding movements. Where specific LOB movements are provided they are year-end gross outstanding balances; the lob_movements field reports year-on-year changes in those gross outstanding balances (2018 vs 2017) as an indicative movement, not a pure prior-year development reconciliation.
